summary: Franz Simon Ferdinand Benary was a religious studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at Bonn and Halle (1824), and completed his habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin (1827) under Franz Bopp, later serving there as lecturer (1829) and extraordinary professor (1831).

Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who completed MA studies at both the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin. He also earned his PhD from the University of Bonn (attested 2003).

Franz von Erdmann (1793–1862) was a linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at the University of Rostock (~1811–1817) and held a post at Kazan Imperial University from approximately 1818 to 1845.

Franz-Karl Ehrhard is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1998) under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Resident Representative for the Nepal Research Centre (1988–1993) and as professor at the University of Munich (2003–2019).
François Gros (1933–2021) was an Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Lyon (~1950–1954) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from approximately 1967 to 2002.

François Lachaud is a scholar in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held posts at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient, including as a professor attested in 2008 and with an affiliation attested in 2013.

Françoise Pommaret is a Tibetologist and historian/archaeologist educated at the Sorbonne, INALCO, and the University of Paris. Her career includes serving as a CNRS directeur de recherche from ~1989 and as Associate Professor and adviser at the Royal University of Bhutan (~2008).

Françoise Robin is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Heather Stoddard at INALCO. She served as a director at the Collège de France (2009–2015) and held departmental leadership posts at INALCO between 2011 and 2014.

Fred Pfeil (1949–2005) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, studying at Amherst College (~1967–1971) and Stanford University (~1971–1973). He taught at Stanford, Stephens College, Oregon State University (~1976–1982), and Trinity College, Hartford (~1983–2005).

Freda Bedi (1911–1977) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at St Hugh's College (~1930–1933) and under Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1953). She founded the Young Lamas Home School and Karma Drubgyu Thargay Ling.

Frederick James Furnivall (1825–1910) was a linguist who studied at University College London and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. He served as Secretary of the Philological Society (1853–1910) and taught at the Working Men's College (~1854–1910).

Frederick M. Asher (1941–2021) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who spent his academic career at the University of Minnesota (~1970–2021), where he served as a professor from around 1980 to 2021.
Frederick M. Smith is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Ludo Rocher. He held a post as professor at the University of Iowa (attested 2006–2008).

Frederick William Thomas (1867–1956) was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied under Edward Byles Cowell at Trinity College, Cambridge. He served as Librarian at the India Office Library (1898–1927) and Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederik David Kan Bosch (1887–1967) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He headed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (~1916–1936) and held academic posts at Utrecht University (1938–1945) and Leiden University (1946–1957).

Fredrik Barth (1928–2016) studied anthropology at Chicago and Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), the University of Oslo (from 1974), and Boston University (~1997–2008).
Friederike Assandri is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. She studied under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer at Heidelberg University, where she was also affiliated as attested in 2013.

Friedhelm Hardy (1943–2004) was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who pursued doctoral work at the University of Oxford (1967). He served as Professor of Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004) and Wilde Lecturer at Oxford (1985–1987).

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff (1928–2009) was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned PhDs at the University of Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University (1964–1982) and Hamburg (1982–1993).

Friedrich August Rosen (1805–1837) was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Franz Bopp. He served as professor of oriental languages at University College London (1828–1831) and professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1834).
